title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye in Tehran
credits: Photos: Unsplash (Tehran, file) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: High-level delegations from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye are in Tehran, trying to stop a new war.
Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, is there, along with Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman.
Türkiye has sent the head of its intelligence service.
According to the Associated Press, they are meeting Iran's top security officials and negotiators, to push for a deal between Tehran and Washington.
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, from Yemen, are also on the agenda.
Saudi Arabia says the aim is to find ways to de-escalate tensions and strengthen regional security.
Iran's foreign ministry says the window of diplomacy has not closed, and messages are being passed to the US through intermediaries.
But it says no Iranian will accept America's demand for complete surrender.
In Israel, Prime Minister Netanyahu says the army is ready both to defend and to strike.
The visit comes days after Pakistan, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Egypt backed the Pakistan-brokered Islamabad MoU between Iran and the US.
With Israel voting on Tuesday and the US on the third of November, the coming days are critical.
